_comment: Single source of truth for the Qt sources that the vendored trees in
were built from. The BOM.json inside each vendored tree is a COPY of this,
written by build-qt-win.ps1 at build time.
It lives here and not in the app repo on purpose: the watcher needs to read
it from a workflow, and GITHUB_TOKEN cannot reach another repository. Making
this the origin instead of reading the app repo removes the cross-repo
token problem and the two-file drift that would come with it.
Commits are PINNED, not the branch tip. That is what makes 'Windows and
Linux ship the same Qt' true by construction instead of true only on the
day someone compiled. These are the commits the Arch Linux package builds

qtbase.note: QMimeDatabase: handle buggy type definitions with circular inheritance

why: The KDE branch commit is NEWER than the 5.15.19 release tag. It carries
upstream commits that landed after that cut as well as the distro
backports, so calling it '5.15.19 + KDE patches' is imprecise: the
version string stays 5.15.19 because Qt does not bump it on the branch.
It is measurably different, not a naming quibble: this tree ships SQLite
3.49.1 and libpng 1.6.47, the official 5.15.19 tarball carries SQLite

vendored.bom: BOM.json inside each tree records this same file's content
